scope: every sense authored in tick 2 (shard 11), drawn complete rather than sampled
authoring: parallel family-author agents, one per family, Opus 5 at xhigh. Each agent read the rubric and the worksheet from disk and wrote its own JSON to disk; no family's content passed through the orchestrating session, which is the fix for the bottleneck census 004 exposed.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool, calculating approval — it rates a thing by the edge it hands you and says nothing about whether that edge is deserved or does any good.
examples: a contract advantageous to our country

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and firmly approving — it credits the thing with actually improving matters, where *advantageous* only counts the edge gained.
examples: an arms limitation agreement beneficial to all countries
the beneficial effects of a temperate climate

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Accusatory where its neighbours approve — it treats the partiality itself as the offence rather than as a favour worth having.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer than *advantageous*: the advantage reads as conditions tilting your way rather than as an edge coldly reckoned up.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The British spelling of *favorable*, carrying the identical tilt-in-your-favour approval with no shift in force.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same claim as *beneficial* stripped of its formality, asserting the benefit flatly instead of arguing for it.
examples: the experience was good for her

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brisk and informal — it books a thing on the credit side without pausing to weigh how much good is in it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Broad and unemphatic approval that places a thing on the good side without naming the advantage, where *beneficial* names it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and administrative: it records that partiality is in play and leaves untouched the question *discriminatory* settles against it.
examples: a preferential shop gives priority or advantage to union members in hiring or promoting

entries.definition: inclined to respect views and beliefs that differ from your own
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm, unhedged praise for a settled disposition, crediting respect for the differing view rather than the bare patience *tolerant* stops at.
examples: a judge who is broad-minded but even-handed

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated almost to neutrality — the same approval as *broad-minded* with the force stripped out of it.

entries.definition: free from provincial prejudices or attachments
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and elevated, praising a sweep wide enough that no narrow attachment survives it.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise with defiance in it — the openness is a refusal of dogma, not the mild receptiveness of *open-minded*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sounds a note of magnanimity, as though the openness were generosity of spirit and not merely fairness.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Bookish and clinical, naming the position where *free-thinking* cheers for it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most expansive term here, praising openness as a governing principle rather than a reaction to any particular view.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain and unpretentious, asking no more than a willingness to hear the new idea out.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The coolest praise in the set — it credits forbearance, granting a view room instead of welcoming it.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defined by what it withholds, measuring out its approval as an absence of rigidity rather than any positive warmth.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The longer, stiffer twin of *undogmatic*, its extra syllable pulling it further from anything conversational.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Shifts from the inner state to the visible one, crediting a confidence you can see in the bearing where *confident* merely records it.
examples: she paints with an assured hand

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Jeering and informal - the excess is not diagnosed but mocked, a swagger the word refuses to take seriously beside the flat *overconfident*.

entries.definition: having or marked by confidence or assurance
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain baseline of the family, reporting that the assurance is there without passing any verdict on whether it is warranted.
examples: his manner is more confident these days

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The straight clinical name for the fault, marking the confidence as more than warranted and leaving the derision to *cocksure*.
examples: so overconfident and impudent as to speak to the queen

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest carrier of that same excess, an everyday word that lets the overreach register as a shrug rather than an accusation.
examples: the less he knows, the more positive he gets

entries.definition: having confidence restored; freed from anxiety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Confidence handed back rather than held all along - the settled calm of anxiety lifted, where the rest of the family says nothing about anything having been shaken.
examples: reassured by her praise he pressed on

entries.definition: showing poise and confidence in your own worth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns the poise inward onto one's own worth and lets it show as composure, steadier-sounding than the bare *confident*.

entries.definition: showing poise and confidence in your own worth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest label for that same belief in one's own worth, stating it where *self-assured* leans on the outward steadiness.
examples: hardly more than a boy but firm-knit and self-confident

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measuring and cool - it rates a resemblance as very close while stopping short of calling it the same thing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and a little grand - closeness with good cheer inside it, heartier than the merely matey *chummy*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The doubled informal form makes the closeness emphatic and knowing where *chummy* keeps it mild.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and light - friendly association on easy terms, without the depth *intimate* claims.
examples: the bartender was chummy with the regular customers

entries.definition: held together as by social or cultural ties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of cohesion - the bond is what holds people together, structural where *dear* is personal.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain measure of nearness in relevance or relationship, stating the proximity without the warmth or the suspicion the rest of the set add.
examples: we are all … in close sympathy with …

entries.definition: held together as by social or cultural ties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The open form spells the binding out and reads more deliberate and descriptive than the compact *close-knit*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Closeness figured as trust - what passes inside it is entrusted, where *chummy* is merely companionable.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling carrying the same imputation of connivance, warmth named in order to be distrusted.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Insinuating - the closeness is treated as connivance, so the snugness of the word becomes the accusation.
examples: a cozy arrangement with the police

entries.definition: with or in a close or intimate relationship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Affectionate and avowed - the close relationship is felt as fondness, where *thick* merely reports the association.
examples: my sisters and brothers are near and dear

entries.definition: having mutual interests or affections; of established friendship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Closeness worn as ease - an established friendship that needs no ceremony, less ardent than *intimate*.

entries.definition: with or in a close or intimate relationship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain and understated for the same close relationship - it vouches for the bond rather than professing feeling as *dear* does.

entries.definition: having mutual interests or affections; of established friendship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest claim in the set - mutual affection and settled friendship, closer and more private than *familiar*.
examples: pretending she is on an intimate footing with those she slanders

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunter than *approximate* for the same degree of resemblance - it asserts the likeness flatly instead of hedging it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt informal shorthand for being closely associated, reporting the tie without the warmth *chummy* supplies.
examples: the two were thick as thieves for months

entries.definition: feeling physical discomfort or pain (‘tough’ is occasionally used colloquially for ‘bad’)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and unspecific about the body feeling wrong, naming neither the site nor the sharpness of what is felt.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States a lack rather than a hurt — the bleakness sits in what is missing, which makes it colder than *uncomfortable*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points at discomfort that nags and chafes, a lower-grade complaint than *painful* though the two name the same effect.
examples: bites of black flies are more than irritating: they can be very painful

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gathers the discomfort into a whole bodily condition instead of a single sensation, so it reads as total rather than local.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heavier word for that same effect, putting the discomfort on the scale of hurt rather than annoyance.
examples: bites of black flies are more than irritating: they can be very painful

entries.definition: feeling physical discomfort or pain (‘tough’ is occasionally used colloquially for ‘bad’)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The colloquial counterpart to *bad*, looser and more offhand about the same felt discomfort.
examples: he was feeling tough after a restless night

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain cover term, working equally for the thing that gives the discomfort and the body that feels it, which is what keeps it so flat.
examples: an uncomfortable day in the hot sun

entries.definition: relating to bodily unease that causes discomfort
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The faintest of these: a bodily unsettledness that has not hardened into pain, more a hint than a hurt.

entries.definition: uncomfortable because of possible danger or trouble
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Locates the discomfort in looming danger or trouble rather than in the flesh, and its mildness is exactly what makes it sound like a warning.
examples: made things warm for the bookies

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A degree past *miserable* on the same misery — abject, with no dignity left to the body it describes.
examples: spent a wretched night on the floor

entries.definition: requiring more than usually expected or thought due; especially great patience and effort and skill
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and unheated - it names the size of what is asked without ruling on whether asking it is fair, where *hard-to-please* has already convicted someone.
examples: a baby can be so demanding

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the weight on the standard itself, so the precision reads as a measure to be met rather than a temper to be humoured.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The formal, cool-surfaced twin of *exacting* - the same insistence on precision, pitched at a distance.
examples: became more exigent over his pronunciation

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disparaging - the fussiness makes the demand a flaw in the person, which *exacting* never does.
examples: his father was a hard-to-please taskmaster

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The open spelling carries the same verdict but reads as a running remark about someone rather than a label fixed to them.

entries.definition: demanding or needing attention, affection, or reassurance to an excessive degree
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Belittling and intimate - the excess is emotional appetite, and the word tips toward pity where *hard-to-please* stays at irritation.

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving - the strictness registers as discipline worth having, where *tight* only pinches.

entries.definition: severe and unremitting in making demands
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds a forbidding manner to the severity - the unrelenting demand arrives with a chill that *strict* does not carry.

entries.definition: severe and unremitting in making demands
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat word for the same unrelenting severity, stating it without colouring it as harshness.

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Cool and administrative, stating how tightly the rules bind without either praising or resenting the binding.

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The informal one, and the constriction is felt - the rules squeeze rather than uphold anything.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Loads the wanting with hunger, so the thing is not merely worth having but longed for hard, far greedier than the flat *in demand*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Relishing rather than clinical, it savours the desire the thing arouses where *sexually attractive* merely reports it.

entries.definition: worth having or seeking or achieving
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The measured, unheated verdict — it says a thing is worth having without claiming anyone is straining after it, which is what *coveted* adds.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a thing by pointing at the sourness it stirs in whoever lacks it, so the approval arrives through someone else's discontent.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: States much-wantedness as a plain fact about a thing's standing, with none of the appetite audible in *coveted*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and relishing, it heaps the desirability higher than the sober *desirable* and sounds pleased with itself for saying so.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A comparative and nothing more — it rates one thing above another without claiming either is wanted much at all.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Settles the comparison that *preferable* is still arguing, presenting the ranking as already decided rather than urged.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Flat and explicit, naming the arousal outright without a trace of the relish in *delectable*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hyphen compresses that same pursuit into a single modifier that can sit in front of the noun it flatters.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the wanting into motion — the thing is actively pursued, where *in demand* leaves it a standing condition.

entries.definition: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving - it treats the full call on your abilities and resources as a reach worth making rather than a weight to be borne.

entries.definition: difficult to accomplish; demanding considerable mental effort and skill
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty - it dwells on the sustained mental effort and skill the thing exacts before it will be accomplished, heavier in the mouth than *hard*.
examples: the arduous work of preparing a dictionary

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildly disapproving - the difficulty sits in the handling, since any move you make risks the pain or embarrassment the thing carries.
examples: awkward (or embarrassing or difficult) moments in the discussion
an awkward pause followed his remark

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the great mental demand where understanding fails - the thing does not merely resist solution, it leaves you at a loss.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Warns of a snare - the difficulty is concealed until you are into it, so the word marks the thing as harder than it lets on.

entries.definition: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns that same full call on everything you have into an invitation to rise to it, so the demand reads as a spur where *problematic* reads as a fault.
examples: performed the most challenging task without a mistake

entries.definition: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unemotive - it registers that effort is required to do, grasp or bear the thing, without hinting whether that effort is worth spending, as *challenging* does.
examples: nesting places on the cliffs are difficult of access

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The difficulty is in the slipping away: comprehension seems within reach and will not close on it, unlike the frank obstruction of *knotty*.

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the discomfort squarely on the face of whoever has to deal with it, naming the exposure that *awkward* leaves implied.
examples: awkward (or embarrassing or difficult) moments in the discussion

entries.definition: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The blunt, plain-spoken version of *difficult* for the same demand, taking effort of body, mind or endurance as it comes and softening none of it.
examples: why is it so hard for you to keep a secret?

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Gives the mental demand a shape - a tangle to be picked apart strand by strand, rather than the blank wall of *baffling*.
examples: I faced the knotty problem of what to have for breakfast

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Labels the demanding thing a problem outright, a mild verdict against it where *tough* only reports the demand.

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stiffer and more formal than *problematic* for the same verdict, its extra syllable adding weight rather than force.

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal - it makes the trouble something you are caught in and cannot step cleanly out of, lighter in tone than *unenviable* and no easier to escape.

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and almost respectful of the difficulty - it sizes up the mental demand as something to be taken on and says nothing against it.

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: An understated verdict that condemns by observation - the thing is framed as unwished-for, and the word damns it without raising its voice.
examples: in the unenviable position of resorting to an act he had planned to save for the climax of the campaign

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and faintly formal, stating the nonexistence with none of the note of shortfall in *lacking*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Bleak - the total lack is a desolate condition rather than the cool fact *devoid* states.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Severe - the complete lack sounds like deprivation, emptiness that hurts.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and absolute, naming total emptiness while passing no verdict on it.
examples: the sentence was devoid of meaning

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The approving member - the same complete lack is a relief, the absent thing one you are better off without.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Light and wry - complete absence made to sound blameless, the opposite colouring to *destitute*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Registers the nonexistence as a deficiency rather than a bare fact, which *absent* does not.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at the gap - the nonexistence is felt as a hole where something belonged.

entries.definition: not having existence or being or actuality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and absolute - the thing simply has no being, without the sense in *missing* that it was expected somewhere.

entries.definition: no longer existing or inaccessible through loss or destruction
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and dry - marks the thing as gone through loss or destruction and judges nothing about it.
examples: its nonextant original was written on vellum

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the drama of a disappearance - existence not merely denied but ended, where *nonexistent* implies no before.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most judging of these - the nonexistence reads as falling short of a mark, not merely as nothing being there.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Steps up from *expensive* to a price high enough to be remarkable, still with no verdict attached to it.
examples: big-ticket items like cars and furs

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Weightier than *high-priced*, the price felt as a cost borne rather than a number quoted.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: British, and softer than *costly* — the same high price delivered in an everyday, conversational word.
examples: much too dear for my pocketbook

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Moves the price off money entirely onto loss or sacrifice, naming what something took without condemning it.

entries.definition: high in price or charging high prices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for a high price, stating the fact without deciding whether the price is deserved.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and purely descriptive: it says the price is high and refuses any attitude toward it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the same very-high price as *big-ticket* in a flatter, more transactional ring.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Judgement rather than measurement — it sets the price against the value and finds it unearned.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and faintly grumbling — the high price registered as a small complaint rather than a measurement.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same informal grumble as *pricey* in a clipped spelling, with no shift in force.

entries.definition: of laws and regulations; designed to protect trade and commerce from unfair business practices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely classificatory - it says what a law or regulation is built to protect trade from, and commends no one.

entries.definition: of laws and regulations; designed to protect trade and commerce from unfair business practices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and as neutral as *antimonopoly*, marking a regulation's protective purpose rather than approving anybody's conduct.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves by negation - nothing foul in the play - where *sportsmanlike* names the virtue outright.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The emphatic one - its doubled phrasing insists there is nothing left to question, where *just* simply states that the standard was met.

entries.definition: of a person; just and impartial; not prejudiced
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a settled cast of mind rather than a single dealing - the impartiality is lodged in the person.

entries.definition: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain, unarguable approval - it certifies that no favoritism or deception got in, without the weight of principle *just* carries.

entries.definition: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Heavier than *fair* - the same absence of bias, but weighted as a standard rightly upheld rather than a condition merely met.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer and easier than *clean*, crediting fair play as a spirit brought to the contest rather than a rule left unbroken.
examples: a sporting solution of the disagreement

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The formal member - it measures conduct against a named standard of sportsmanship instead of merely reporting, as *clean* does, that nothing foul happened.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most casual of these, informal and light, granting the same approval with none of *sportsmanlike*'s weight.
examples: a sporting solution of the disagreement

entries.definition: having more than the average number of accidents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildly damning - it turns a count of mishaps into a standing property of whatever it is aimed at, so the accidents read as owed to it rather than to chance.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral but predictive - it treats the leaning as a matter of the subject's nature, so what follows sounds expected rather than merely possible.
examples: he is apt to ignore matters he considers unimportant

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and dry - the leaning sounds like a settled arrangement of temperament rather than an appetite, cooler than *given*.

entries.definition: (followed by ‘of’ or ‘to’) having a strong preference or liking for
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Warm - the leaning is felt as liking rather than as mere direction, which is what lifts it clear of *inclined*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and settled - the disposition sounds ingrained rather than merely present, heavier and more everyday than *disposed*.

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘to’) having a preference, disposition, or tendency
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Mild and non-committal - the leaning is stated lightly enough to leave room for doing otherwise, where *prone* fixes it in place.
examples: wasn't inclined to believe the excuse

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the disposition in the subject's cast of mind rather than in what it does, which is what separates it from *tending*.
examples: I am not minded to answer any questions

entries.definition: (followed by ‘of’ or ‘to’) having a strong preference or liking for
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Lighter and more indulgent than *fond* - it casts the strong liking as a weakness cheerfully admitted.

entries.definition: having a tendency (to); often used in combination
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and fixing - it states the tendency as a standing liability rather than a leaning, and welds straight onto whatever is tended toward.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest of these - it names the direction of the leaning and claims nothing about temperament or liking.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The barest approval here - it grants appeal to the mind without characterizing that appeal at all.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes the cultivation conspicuous, so the compliment carries an edge *intellectual* does not.
examples: highbrow events such as the ballet or opera

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same claim to high cultivation as *highbrow*, but the participial form sits heavier and stiffer.

entries.definition: appealing to or using the intellect
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain term of the family - it names the faculty being engaged and passes no verdict on it.
examples: intellectual workers engaged in creative literary or artistic or scientific labor
has tremendous intellectual sympathy for oppressed people

entries.definition: having its source in or being guided by the intellect (as distinguished from experience or emotion)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional rather than approving - it places the source of the thinking in the intellect as against experience.

entries.definition: devoted to matters of the mind
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Quieter and warmer than *intellectual* - a mind given over to its own concerns rather than one showing power.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weightier than *good* for the same appeal to the mind, casting it as demanding rather than merely worth having.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of these - it treats appeal to the intellect as refinement rather than plain substance.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Regard rather than warmth - the approval answers to what the object is, so it can be offered coolly and from a distance.

entries.definition: regarded with deep or rapturous love (especially as if for a god)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Love at its most rapturous, pitched as high as devotion to a god and far past anything *loved* claims.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and settled - it names the one dearly loved instead of reporting a feeling, which gives it a weight *darling* has none of.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names the favorite by an image rather than by any word for feeling, so the approval reads as preference rather than passion.

entries.definition: characterized by feeling or showing fond affection for
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Fond affection with tending in it - the feeling is kept up, not merely felt.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Fond and light, dear love spoken as endearment; it can be said playfully where *beloved* cannot.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The quiet, unemphatic way to say dearly loved - small in sound and large in meaning.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Marks the one singled out for favor - flattering about standing, not about the depth of love in *adored*.
examples: the fair-haired boy of the literary set

entries.definition: regarded with deep or rapturous love (especially as if for a god)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same raising of the loved one into an object of worship, love felt as reverence rather than as fondness.

entries.definition: regarded with deep or rapturous love (especially as if for a god)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sets the loved one above the lover - rapture that looks up at what it loves.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word for holding dear, stating the fact of the feeling without measuring its heat, where *adored* measures nothing else.
examples: his loved companion of many years

entries.definition: characterized by feeling or showing fond affection for
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns fond affection into worth, so the one held is valued as much as loved.

entries.definition: characterized by feeling or showing fond affection for
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Affection that hoards - what is felt fondly is also kept and guarded, where *cherished* only tends it.

entries.definition: characterized by feeling or showing fond affection for
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest of these - fond affection showing itself as desire for the one held, with none of the ceremony of *treasured*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A figurative way of calling someone the favorite: approval that consists in being picked out.

entries.definition: regarded with deep or rapturous love (especially as if for a god)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: States outright the comparison the others only lean on: love offered as if to a god.

entries.definition: involving the entire earth; not limited or provincial in scope
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unmarked word for whole-earth extent, and the one that sets that extent against the narrow and the provincial.

entries.definition: concerning or belonging to all or at least two or more nations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and minimal in its demand — two nations are enough to satisfy it, where *global* asks for the whole earth.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names a commitment rather than an extent — it says where someone stands, not how far something reaches, as *international* does.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The longer form, stiffer and more label-like than *internationalist* without adding to the stance it names.

entries.definition: involving or operating in several nations or nationalities
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and countable — several nations or nationalities added together, where *international* needs only a relation between two.

entries.definition: involving the entire earth; not limited or provincial in scope
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Covers the same whole-earth extent as *global* but with a grander, more astronomical ring to it.
examples: neither national nor continental but planetary

entries.definition: transcending established national boundaries or spheres of interest
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Sets the thing above national boundaries and interests rather than merely across them, a step beyond *transnational*.

entries.definition: involving or operating in several nations or nationalities
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Frames the same several-nation range as crossing the lines rather than summing them up, as *multinational* does.

entries.definition: involving the entire earth; not limited or provincial in scope
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The hyphenated form of *worldwide*, identical in force and a shade more deliberate on the page.

entries.definition: involving the entire earth; not limited or provincial in scope
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bare noun pressed into adjective duty, flat and workmanlike where *global* sounds considered.

entries.definition: involving the entire earth; not limited or provincial in scope
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the weight on reach stretching across the earth rather than on the earth as a single whole, which *global* implies.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Absolute rather than pointed - the condemnation is total in degree where *nasty* keeps a needling edge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contempt by way of defilement - it treats what it hits as unclean rather than merely offensive, a heavier verdict than *grotty*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The disgust in *dirty* pushed to its limit, vileness so thorough it lands as a moral verdict.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and slangy, it registers offensiveness as squalid distaste rather than the moral condemnation in *filthy*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes ill will the whole of the charge, naming the malice itself where *nasty* only shades toward it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contempt thrown off casually - the despising is real but carries none of the weight that *filthy* brings to it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word for malice, stating the ill will flatly where *hateful* makes it sound monstrous.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns without naming the fault, covering plain offensiveness and shading into outright ill will, where *hateful* puts the malice at the centre.
examples: Will he say nasty things at my funeral?

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The lightest way here of saying the thing shows itself — it reports the showing rather than pressing it, unlike *unmistakable*.
examples: the effects of the drought are apparent to anyone who sees the parched fields

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and absolute — the thing stands with no argument put behind it, a larger claim than being merely *evident*.

entries.definition: capable of being demonstrated or proved
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Shifts from what is seen to what can be shown: the clarity is available on demand rather than immediate, unlike *obvious*.
examples: a demonstrable lack of concern for the general welfare

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and unemphatic: the thing is simply there to be seen, with none of the display *manifest* makes of it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and unemphatic — it flags the thing as clearly there and does nothing more with it, where *manifest* makes a display.

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and expansive — the thing does not merely show but puts itself on show, a grander word than *evident* for the same clarity.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat baseline of the group: a thing takes no effort to see or grasp, without *palpable*'s pressure or *axiomatic*'s claim about proof.

entries.definition: so obvious as to be easily solved or decided
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and conclusive: the obviousness is enough to settle the matter, not merely to be seen — a force *plain* never reaches.

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pushes the showing towards touch, so the thing is felt as much as seen — heavier in the hand than *apparent*.

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and declarative: the clarity is stated as settled fact rather than offered as an impression, where *palpable* appeals to the senses.

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The homeliest word here — clarity with no ceremony at all, exactly what *manifest* supplies in excess.
examples: it is plain that he is no reactionary

entries.definition: capable of being demonstrated or proved
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The blunter twin of *demonstrable*, resting the whole claim on proof being possible.
examples: practical truth provable to all men

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainer word for the same standing as *axiomatic*: the thing carries its own warrant and asks for none to be brought.
examples: we hold these truths to be self-evident

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The thing supplies its own account, so nothing need be added to it — a different job from *obvious*, which only says it is easy to grasp.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: An ordinary-language phrase that concedes the standing rather than asserting it — the thing passes without argument instead of being shown to need none.

entries.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Works by ruling out the alternative: the thing cannot be read as anything else, a firmer guarantee than *apparent* gives.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt - concealment is not just absent but conspicuously unattempted, and the missing softening reads as harshness.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Accusatory where *bald* is merely blunt - the failure to conceal registers as nerve, something the doer should have been ashamed to show.

entries.definition: devoid of elaboration or diminution or concealment; bare and pure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Stark - nothing added and nothing subtracted, so the thing stands in its own unsoftened proportions.

entries.definition: open and observable; not secret or hidden
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain everyday word for the same state, weightless where *overt* sounds like a term of art.

entries.definition: open and observable; not secret or hidden
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and formal - it marks a thing as out where it can be seen and stops there, with none of the affront *barefaced* adds.

entries.definition: devoid of elaboration or diminution or concealment; bare and pure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Coarser-grained than *naked* - unworked rather than merely stripped, with the roughness of the thing left on it.
examples: you may kill someone someday with your raw power

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names concealment in order to deny it, so what is plain to see carries the sense of something that could have been hidden and was not.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely descriptive and the mildest of the set - it reports what the eye catches, without implying anything was ever kept back.

entries.definition: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Faintly flattering, since calling something intellectual credits it with demanding real thought, where *mental* says no more than that the mind was involved.

entries.definition: involving the mind or an intellectual process
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest of these, taking in any process the mind performs without the technical precision *psychological* carries.

entries.definition: psychological rather than physical or tangible in effect
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names not the mind itself but the kind of effect that lands there, real in force with nothing tangible behind it.

entries.definition: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most abstract and learned of the set, naming mind-work in a lofty register that *mental* keeps flat.

entries.definition: affecting or influenced by the human mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reaches in both directions at once, covering what the mind acts on and what acts on the mind, where *psychogenic* narrows to where a thing began.

entries.definition: affecting or influenced by the human mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The heavier, more formal twin of *psychic*, identical in what it covers and stiffer in the saying.

entries.definition: mental or emotional rather than physiological in origin
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and exact about causation, placing the starting point in the mind rather than the body instead of merely sorting by nature.

entries.definition: mental or emotional as opposed to physical in nature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The workaday technical term here, sorting a thing by what it is in nature rather than, as *psychogenic* does, by where it came from.

entries.definition: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at the mind as the faculty at work rather than at the soundness of what it produces, making it a label and not a verdict.
examples: the triumph of the rational over the animal side of man

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval with esteem in it - it asks you to look up at the thing rather than merely enjoy it, a graver register than *charming*.
examples: among her many admirable qualities are generosity and graciousness

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and disarming - the pleasure sounds like an appeal exerted on you, gentler than *delightful*'s enthusiasm.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Savouring - it makes high pleasure sound like something relished, richer and more indulgent than *delightful*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enthusiastic - the pleasure is raised to a high pitch and given an edge of entertainment that *pleasing* lacks.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated to the edge of neutrality - it concedes that pleasure is afforded without any warmth of praise behind it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Slangy and clipped - the same top-of-the-scale praise as *fabulous*, tossed off rather than declared.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Extravagant - praise pitched at the ceiling and past plausibility, far louder than *pleasing*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: All-purpose and colourless - it grants no more than the capacity to please, where *pleasing* reports pleasure actually given.

entries.definition: pleasing to the mind or feeling
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sober and faintly formal - it puts the pleasure in the mind or the feelings rather than on the surface, weightier than *sweet*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: It measures pleasing by the favour won rather than by the pleasure given, which tilts it away from praising the thing at all, unlike *charming*.
examples: with open arms and an ingratiating smile

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain, unraised approval - it states the pleasure and satisfaction given and leaves it there, where *delightful* insists.

entries.definition: pleasing to the mind or feeling
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and informal - the same inward pleasure as *gratifying*, but tender and unguarded rather than composed.

entries.definition: not modified or restricted by reservations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and clipped, it shuts the door on reservations like a ruling handed down, where *unqualified* merely reports that there are none.

entries.definition: not modified or restricted by reservations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unclipped form of *categoric*, and the extra syllable lands as extra weight: reservations are not merely absent but refused.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Faintly approving — freedom from qualifications felt as tidiness, nothing left clinging, where *unqualified* only records that nothing is attached.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same freedom as *clean*, but as an unobstructed way through rather than a tidy finish: nothing in the way rather than nothing left over.

entries.definition: not modified or restricted by reservations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and monosyllabic — the refusal of reservations delivered as a door shutting, where *categorical* delivers it as a pronouncement.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Emphatic and forceful, it presses the thing all the way through with no exception admitted, well past *unqualified*'s bare report.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and plain-spoken, it admits no reservation or exception exactly as *outright* does, but without the ceremony.

entries.definition: not modified or restricted by reservations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and absolute, it presents the missing reservations as terms deliberately not imposed rather than as *flat*'s curt refusal to entertain them.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reads as sheer extent — nothing bounds the thing — where *outright* reads as manner, nothing qualifying it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare statement of the case — nothing limits or restricts the thing — with none of the insistence *categorical* puts behind it.

entries.definition: capable of thinking and expressing yourself in a clear and consistent manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise at its lowest setting: the thought holds together and comes out clear, a floor cleared rather than the brightness *lucid* claims.
examples: she was more coherent than she had been just after the accident

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries no more judgment than *demythologized*: the stripping of myth is stated, not celebrated or mourned.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatly descriptive - records that the mythical element is gone without approving or regretting its removal.

entries.definition: endowed with the capacity to reason
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns the bare endowment into a compliment, where *reasoning* and *thinking* only register that the capacity is there.

entries.definition: capable of thinking and expressing yourself in a clear and consistent manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dry, near-technical commendation - the clear consistent thinking treated as something that works by rule, with none of *lucid*'s warmth.

entries.definition: capable of thinking and expressing yourself in a clear and consistent manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of the three: the same clear consistent thinking praised as brightness, where *coherent* merely reports that it hangs together.

entries.definition: consistent with or based on or using reason
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves by pointing at the grounds - the thing rests on reason - where *reasonable* praises the quality of the judgment actually reached.

entries.definition: marked by sound judgment; having good reason
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Solid approval of judgment exercised well, going past *rational*'s weaker claim that reason was involved at all.

entries.definition: endowed with the capacity to reason
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely descriptive - states that the faculty is present and stops, extending none of the credit *intelligent* does for it.

entries.definition: marked by sound judgment; having good reason
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same sound judgment, but pitched as the bar a mind must clear rather than a distinction it earns, which gives it a weight *reasonable* has not.

entries.definition: endowed with the capacity to reason
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral in the way *reasoning* is, marking the capacity as a plain attribute rather than a merit.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Cool and measuring — it grants acceptability and stops there, withholding the warmth *fine* carries.
examples: more than adequate as a secretary

entries.definition: being satisfactory or in satisfactory condition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A plain all-clear — it reports that nothing is amiss rather than that anything is good, a smaller claim than *copacetic* makes.
examples: the passengers were shaken up but are all right

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same untroubled sufficiency in a spelling flagged as nonstandard, and that flag is the whole of what separates it from *all right*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Raises rather than soothes: it clears worry by lifting the spirits, where *comforting* clears it by settling them.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and aimed at the worrier — it quiets a mind rather than removing what alarmed it, softer than the lift in *cheering*.

entries.definition: being satisfactory or in satisfactory condition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Slangy assent that approves by declining to object; the ease is the point, where *fine* merely settles the matter.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Slangy and total — it closes off every remaining objection, where *all right* reports only that none has surfaced.
examples: his smile said that everything was copacetic
You had to be a good judge of what a man was like, and the English was copacetic

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A colloquial shrug whose own hedging spreads the verdict between fair and middling instead of landing on either.

entries.definition: being satisfactory or in satisfactory condition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brisk and unqualified: one syllable that closes the question of whether the thing will do, with none of *satisfactory*'s weighing.
examples: dinner and the movies had been fine
another minute I'd have been fine

entries.definition: being satisfactory or in satisfactory condition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Breezy slang whose bounce overshoots the modest thing it reports — all is in order, announced as though it were a delight.

entries.definition: being satisfactory or in satisfactory condition
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The barest possible grant of sufficiency — two letters conceding the thing is in order, without a particle of the warmth in *fine*.

entries.definition: being satisfactory or in satisfactory condition
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The spelled-out form, sitting in a sentence as a word rather than a mark, with the same flat sufficiency as *ok*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Acceptance with the bar still visible underneath it: the thing gets through, where *adequate* says it measures up.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval delivered as a finding rather than a compliment — it certifies that satisfaction was given, where *fine* simply grants it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Relief supplied by sufficiency itself — the worry lifts because the thing proves enough, where *comforting* works on the person instead.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most grudging of these acceptances, framing the acceptable thing as something borne, where *passable* at least lets it through clean.

entries.definition: low or inferior in station or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names low station with a quiet grace, so the lowness reads as unpretending rather than deficient.

entries.definition: fairly poor to not very good
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Damns by withholding: it refuses praise rather than delivering a charge, and the refusal is the verdict.
examples: has indifferent qualifications for the job

entries.definition: of or characteristic of low rank or importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The bare comparative of the set: it grades a thing below others and lets the ranking itself carry the sting, where *humble* names the same position without grading it.

entries.definition: at a low level in rank or importance
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely positional, marking a rung on a scale of rank without judging the worth of whatever stands there.

entries.definition: low or inferior in station or quality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt monosyllable for that station, stating the bottom position flatly and with none of the softening in *humble*.

entries.definition: low or inferior in station or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Adds a meek, faintly literary air to the low position, so it sounds borne rather than merely recorded.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A coordinate rather than a verdict, fixing a point between top and bottom and claiming nothing about quality.

entries.definition: low or inferior in station or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The tactful word for the same lowness, declining to call it poor and leaving the thing its dignity.
examples: a modest man of the people

entries.definition: decisively surpassed by something else so as to appear to be of a lower class
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The strongest of the set: the low standing is the outcome of a contest already decisively lost, so the word carries the humiliation of the comparison.

entries.definition: low or inferior in station or quality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shrinks rather than ranks, so the low quality registers as insignificance instead of a place on a ladder.

entries.definition: conforming to fact and therefore worthy of belief
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The belief is earned by checking out against the facts, so the praise is for genuineness rather than for any goodwill.
examples: an authentic account by an eyewitness

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Technical and bloodless, certifying a bar cleared rather than praising anything about the one who cleared it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise for weight-bearing steadiness - it promises the thing will hold, where *authentic* only says it is what it claims.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and classifying - it marks a thing as resting on trust without any opinion on whether that trust is deserved.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer and broader than *dependable*, resting the approval on the whole character rather than on any record of performance.

entries.definition: conforming to fact and therefore worthy of belief
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sober and unexcited - it credits a thing with holding up under scrutiny and claims nothing more stirring than that.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A quiet nod at financial standing, softer and less procedural-sounding than *creditworthy* though it settles the same question.

entries.definition: (of persons) worthy of trust or confidence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Blunt and unqualified, the whole verdict compressed into one syllable that leaves no room for hedging.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Elevated and absolute - constancy raised to a virtue, with a solemn ring that *dependable* never reaches for.
examples: he was true to his word
I would be true for there are those who trust me

entries.definition: (of persons) worthy of trust or confidence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The participle makes the standing something conferred, where *sure* names a quality the person carries on their own.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain, unhedged verdict of the family - approval stated flatly, with no warmth or ceremony added to it.
examples: an experienced and trustworthy traveling companion

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving with a homely, affectionate warmth that *trustworthy* keeps out, and a faint pat on the head with it.
examples: an experienced and trustworthy traveling companion
